gist: **The core negative result.** DEER distance distributions for the TM4–TM6 and TM4–TM5 spin pairs, apo vs saturating ZP3780, with the reliability limits for distance and width drawn as bars
data_shape: `PLOT \| facet: spin-label pair (2: TM4–TM6 = 265C/345C, TM4–TM5 = 265C/335C) \| vary: interspin distance, 15–65 Å (continuous) \| series: condition (2: apo shown as gray shading, +ZP3780 shown as a red line) \| measure: probability (area-normalized distance distribution) \| mark: line + filled area \| n: NOT REPORTED — no replicate count is given for any DEER trace, in the caption, the text or the methods`

hides: **Yes, three ways, and one matters for how strongly the null can be read.** (i) **No n and no uncertainty**: unlike every other panel in the paper, the DEER distributions carry no SEM, no confidence band from the Tikhonov/model-free fit, and no replicate count — for a *null* result, the absence of an uncertainty envelope is exactly what a reader needs to judge whether "no change" means "no change above noise". (ii) **The apo and agonist traces use different visual encodings** (filled gray area vs unfilled red line), which makes small differences hard to see in the direction that favours the paper's conclusion. (iii) The **reliability ceiling bars are drawn but never explained in the text** — see `metric_saturation`. The corresponding HDL-particle repeat, which is the control for the detergent artefact, is exiled to fig. S7C

gist: Bimane/NBD emission spectra for GCGR and β<sub>2</sub>AR across apo, +agonist, +agonist+G<sub>s</sub>, and +nucleotide conditions — the fluorescence half of the same argument

(ii) The fluorophore differs between the two receptors in E vs F (NBD for GCGR, bimane for β<sub>2</sub>AR), stated in the text as a sensitivity choice (p.9) but easy to miss; the panels are laid out as if they were the same measurement. hides: No error bars anywhere — FEP+ R² carries cycle-closure and statistical uncertainty that is not drawn, so bar-height differences of 0.05 (the hatching threshold) are shown as if exact. Ligand count per series is not shown, so each bar's weight is invisible. The 13 series that failed the retrospective screen are absent from the figure entirely, and series indices are unlabelled by receptor, so the reader cannot map a bar to a target without Table S1 (**not held**). "Best" model per arm is a maximum over 5 (Boltz) or 25 (IFD-MD) candidates and the figure gives no hint of the distribution it maximised over
